sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Establishment**: Launched in **2015-16** to bridge the gap between the needs of vulnerable states and available funding.
• **Funding Mechanism**: It is a **Central Sector Scheme** with 100% central grant assistance.
• **Nodal Agency**: **NABARD** (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) acts as the National Implementing Entity (NIE).
• **Strategic Alignment**: Projects must be aligned with the **State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC)** and the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Climate-Resilient Agriculture**: Promoting drought-resistant crops and micro-irrigation.
• **Water Security**: Watershed management and restoration of traditional water bodies.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Limited budgetary allocation compared to the scale of climate vulnerability; delays in project approval.
• **Solutions**: Scaling up private sector participation and integrating climate-resilient infrastructure into mainstream development.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'N-A-F-C-C' -> **N**ABARD **A**dapts **F**unds for **C**limate **C**hange.
• **Decoded Meaning**: N (NABARD), A (Adaptation), F (Fund), C (Climate), C (Change).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses NAFFC with the Green Climate Fund (GCF). Remember: NAFFC is domestic (India-specific), while GCF is international (UNFCCC-linked).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Climate-Resilient Development' and 'Bottom-up Adaptation' when discussing NAFFC in the context of India's NDC commitments.

keyTakeaways: NAFFC is a 100% Central Sector Scheme.
NABARD is the exclusive National Implementing Entity.
Projects must align with SAPCC and NAPCC to be eligible for funding.
